title: immediately.run viewer component manifest
description: The component vocabulary a directory-as-content VIEWER declares. Two-way surface (PLATFORM_LAYERING_SPEC §5 target 3): a corpus checker reads it to know which components a corpus may use, and a thin shell composing the viewer as a library (§1.1 M3) reads it to know which components it may override, with what props. The FORMAT is viewer-generic — a Lodestar manifest with a node/edge vocabulary validates through this same schema; only the entries are per-viewer.

name.description: The package name a shell imports.

kind.description: The content kind this viewer renders (`wiki`, `board`, …) — display and discovery only; it confers nothing.

task.description: The task CONTRACT this viewer provides, matching package.json `immediately.run.provides`.

components.description: Component name → its contract. A name absent here is INTERNAL: a corpus using it is flagged, and a shell overriding it fails visibly.

tier.description: `engine` renders any corpus and holds no opinion about its subject; `chrome` is site furniture a layout arranges; `corpus` is furniture encoding ONE corpus's frontmatter conventions, declared by that corpus rather than the engine (ENGINE_BOUNDARY §3).

overridable.description: Whether a library-composing shell may replace it. False for components whose behaviour is engine mechanics rather than presentation.

sanitizing.description: Whether this component is a sanitizing wrapper on the interpreter path. An override of a sanitizing component inherits the obligation — that is why the flag is on the contract and not in a comment.

props.description: Prop name → a short type string (`string?`, `number?`, `node?`, `string[]?`). Documentation for an overriding shell, not a runtime check.

frontmatter.description: Frontmatter key OWNERSHIP (PLATFORM_LAYERING §5 target 1). Each side validates the keys it owns; pass-through is what keeps a foreign corpus with its own vocabulary renderable.

engine.description: Keys the ENGINE reads. Changing one changes rendering.

corpusTooling.description: Keys a corpus's own tooling reads. The engine ignores them.

passThrough.description: Whether unknown keys are allowed (they are carried, unread). False makes the vocabulary closed.

layouts.description: The layout-starters catalogue (R3-309, bucket A): `_layout.mdx` starters under `content/_layouts/` a contributor or agent copies from. Keyed by starter id (= filename); `layoutRole` is the declared kind the entry and the file must agree on — the field existed in the sample layouts for a year with nothing reading it, and the catalogue is what gives it a job.

layoutRole.description: `root` is an outermost shell (selects the nav arrangement); `section` nests under a root and wraps one folder.

arranges.description: The chrome the starter arranges around `<Outlet/>`.

ships.description: Whether the starter file exists today (kept false for a catalogue entry whose file lands with a later item).

collections.description: The collection-shapes catalogue (R3-309, bucket C): what a LIST of entries looks like. Behaviour lives here, not in a starter — an `_layout.mdx` cannot hold state, so infinite scroll is an engine component's literal prop, never a file you copy.

component.description: The engine component the shape rides on (absent for shapes that are not component calls at all — a directory URL is one).

props.description: The literal attributes a corpus writes to select the shape. Expression props are dropped silently by the interpreter — every documented call must stay literal.

ships.description: Whether the shape renders today; a not-yet-shipping entry documents what lands with which item.
